answer: Before an agent can claim a daily subsidy, require a fresh sequential delay proof tied to its key and yesterday's unpredictable beacon. A comet tracking service and a harbor trader face the same serial computation; changing a sable avatar does not reuse either proof. Verify proofs cheaply, expire them at the deadline, and reject repeated key-day claims. A thousand aliases need a thousand parallel computing lanes for the whole delay, not one copied answer. This prices identity multiplication in hardware and time, but cannot prove distinct ownership.
